Free keeps the starter learning loop: basic text practice, word trainer, notes, phrase audio, and progress. Premium opens AI Tutor with listening practice, pronunciation scoring, voice review, image tools, and higher daily limits. Platinum is for dense study with the maximum limits.
Free is enough to test the route and keep a small daily habit.
Premium is the normal daily mode when you need guided lessons, voice, listening, and pronunciation feedback.
Platinum is useful before travel, work, exams, or any period where you practice heavily every day.
Open Premium to compare current prices, payment methods, activation keys, and active status.
The theme toggle changes the whole web interface: background, menu icons, panels, dialogs, login visuals, and contrast. Brightness adjusts the app surface without changing your learning data.
Use the sun/moon control in the top bar or mobile quick controls to switch light and dark themes.
Settings also control interface language, learning language, level, and global learning focus.
Global learning focus guides new lessons and practice topics, so the app stops jumping to random themes.
Theme is visual; language, level, and learning focus affect future content.

A word does not become learned after one click. New words first go to review and spelling practice; they enter the learned vocabulary after enough correct answers, including the 10-correct-answer mastery rule used by the bot.
Use Learn words for new cards, Review game for choices, and Spelling when you need to type from memory.
If a word or translation is wrong, report it from the AI Tutor word report button so the correction reaches the review flow.
Mistakes are grouped by grammar, word order, vocabulary, politeness, and spelling, then trained separately.
Do not chase a huge list. Repeat fewer words correctly until they become stable.

After lessons and practice, save useful answers, corrections, and translations to Notes. Audio buttons let you listen to messages and examples again; pronunciation and listening modes compare what you heard or said.
Save lesson answers to Notes when they are phrases you will actually reuse.
Use Listening to hear a phrase first, repeat it, then check the weak words instead of reading the target immediately.
Use bug reports for interface issues and word reports for wrong vocabulary, translations, or lesson words.
A strong loop is: listen, answer, save the best phrase, report bad data, repeat the weak spot.
